newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul court jails Hanbo patriarch for 15 years.
newsitem.headline: Seoul court jails Hanbo patriarch for 15 years.

text.p: The patriarch of South Korea's troubled Hanbo Group was jailed for 15 years on Monday after he was convicted of bribing top aides to President Kim Young-sam, bankers and others in a scandal that rocked the nation.
Chung Tae-soo was one of 10 people handed stiff prison sentences by a Seoul court in a loans-for-kickbacks scandal involving Hanbo's failed steelmaking flagship.
The others are a former cabinet minister, three lawmakers with the ruling New Korea Party and one with the main opposition party, three ex-bankers and Chung's son, who is Hanbo's current chairman.
The elder Chung, 74, was convicted of giving bribes, embezzlement and fraud. His son, Chung Bo-keun, was jailed for three years for embezzlement.
Father and son were found guilty of siphoning off a combined 364 billion won ($408 million) from funds belonging to the country's 14th largest business group.

The bribes to bankers and politicians were to keep money rolling in to Hanbo Steel Co, which collapsed in January under debts of five trillion won ($5.6 billion), setting off a chain of corporate failures and shaking the banking system.
The scandal shattered President Kim's credibility and unearthed other bribery scandals that led to the arrest of his son, Kim Hyun-chul.

A related flap over Kim Young-sam's spending on his 1992 election campaign, which opposition parties say was bankrolled in part by Hanbo, has sparked a wave of violence by students demanding the president step down.

"Your wrongdoing has caused great shock to the Korean people, harm to the country's economy and chaos in society," chief judge Son Ji-yol told the ailing Chung Tae-soo, who hobbled into court supported by a prison officer.
The court heard that Chung Tae-soo, who suffered a mild stroke after his arrest, handed out cash hidden beneath apples in wooden crates. The lawmakers admitted taking his money, but not as bribes.
Former home affairs minister Kim Woo-suk was jailed for four years.

Lawmaker Hong In-gil of the ruling New Korea Party was sentenced to seven years and his colleagues Hwang Byung-tai and Chung Jae-chull each to three years. Hong was fined one billion won, the stiffest fine handed down to those convicted of accepting bribes.
Another member of the National Assembly, Kwon Roh-kap of the main opposition National Congress for New Politics, was handed a five-year prison term. His lawyers said he would appeal.
Two former presidents of Korea First Bank, Sheen Kwang-shik and Rhee Chul-soo, were jailed for four years and five years, respectively. The bank was the largest creditor to Hanbo Steel.
The one-time president of Chohung Bank, Woo Chan-mok, was jailed for four years.
Hanbo's former financial controller was given a 2-1/2 year jail term suspended for four years.
Chung Tae-soo has been embroiled in corruption scandals twice previously.

In 1991, he was handed a three-year suspended jail term for his role in a real estate scandal. He was convicted last year of bribing former president Roh Tae-woo, but a suspended jail term was thrown out on appeal over a legal technicality.
Eight other politicians were indicted last month on charges of taking bribes from Chung, among them the mayor of Pusan, the country's second largest city.
